A very warm welcome to Minety C of E Primary School
Minety Church of England Primary School is unwavering in its commitment to delivering an unparalleled educational journey for every student. We pride ourselves on our unique curriculum, meticulously crafted to ensure that each child flourishes academically, socially, and personally.
Our dedication extends beyond the traditional subjects of reading, writing, and mathematics. Through a vibrant array of clubs, educational trips, community engagements and participation in sporting events, we provide enriching experiences that contribute to the holistic development of our pupils. Our innovative approach to playtimes further enhances these opportunities for growth.
The guiding values of Integrity, Aspiration, Resilience, Inclusion, Thankfulness, and Respect are at the heart of our school ethos. These values not only foster outstanding learners but also nurture responsible, compassionate individuals who will become exemplary adults.
Our philosophy is encapsulated in the belief that "together, we flourish." This principle underscores all our initiatives, ensuring a supportive and collaborative environment where every child can thrive.

Vision and Values
During the academic year of 2022 and 2023 Minety C of E Primary School looked again at our school vision and values. It is important for schools to do this regularly to ensure that they continue to offer a school that is what is needed for the community at that time.
The full vision and values document can be found here. Information on our Vision and Values
During the process of looking at our vision and values we started by streamling our core values to ensure that as we teach them to children they are able to speak with knowledge and understanding about them. Through working with children, staff and parents we chose Integrity, Aspiration, Resilience, Inclusion, Thankfulness and Respect as our core values.
Over arching our core values is the vision of the school ‘together, we flourish’. This was chosen because, as a school, we are full of wonderful individuals who are unique and each able to achieving alone, however, if we work collectively as a school community we believe that ‘together, we flourish', more than we would if we worked alone.
As a C of E School, we have also underpinned our vision with the Bible Verse:
Ecclesiastes 4:9-10: “Two are better off than one, because together they can work more effectively. If one of them falls down, the other can help them up."
We use our vision and values across our school day. We weave their direct teaching into collective worships and registration time. We celebrate successes in our Golden Book assembly with a focus on one of the different values and as we start to build a curriculum for the children of Minety we will wave our Vision and Values throughout it.

Extra Savings with Tax-Free Childcare: Did you know you can pay for our after-school club using the government’s Tax-Free Childcare scheme? Find out more and check your eligibility here.
Questions or Support? If you need more information or help with booking, please email Mrs Henderson at admin@minety.wilts.sch.uk. We’re happy to help! We can’t wait to welcome your child to our new and improved after-school club—where every day is an adventure!

Governors
The role of the governing body is to oversee and support the school in providing the best possible education for its pupils. School governors set the school's aims and policies together with the Headteacher, who is responsible for the day-to-day management of the school. Governors have responsibilities in such areas as curriculum, finance, personnel, the school building and premises, as well as for the school's provision regarding special educational needs. The governing body as a whole is responsible for any decisions made on behalf of the school.
Anyone interested in finding out more about becoming a school governor should contact the Clerk, Georgina Pilley via the school office.

Leave of absence
Since September 2013, the government announced that all holidays taken during term time would be recorded as unauthorised absence. Please see the latest information produced by the Local Authority to comply with these new regulations.
PUPIL LEAVE OF ABSENCE IN TERM TIME
Important notice to all parents and carers
The Local Authority has amended its Local Code of Conduct in respect of Penalty Notices issued for truancy to include unauthorised pupil leave of absence in term time. If a pupil accumulates 10 or more sessions of unauthorised leave of absence within the previous 6 month period of a current academic year, the school must notify the Local Authority and a Penalty Notice will be issued to each parent for each child where that applies.
A penalty of £60 will apply if paid within 21 days or £120 up to 28 days. If after 28 days the penalty has not been paid, legal proceedings will be taken through the magistrates court for the unauthorised absence.
Please click here to download a leave of absence request form or here to submit an online request.

Snow Procedures
SNOW, GLORIOUS SNOW! In the event of Snow:
We will only close the school if a substantial amount of snow falls making it unsafe for children and staff to travel to school. How to find out if the school is closed:
INFORMATION MESSAGES
WEBSITE - It often takes a lot of time for messages to be posted on the website due to the overwhelming number of schools nationally attempting to put messages on via the Website provider. A message will be posted as soon as possible.
HOME CONTACT – This is our quickest method of getting information to you. Make sure the office have your details so that you can receive a text and at a later pointe an E mail. Details are not disclosed to other parents.
RADIO – Heart FM and BBC Wiltshire will publish a list of schools that are closed. This does, however, take time due to the large number of schools contacting them.
NOTICE ON THE GATE – Failing anything else a message will be put on the gate. For those of you who live in the village – if you have not picked up a message you can, if you walk to the school see this notice.
Should snow fall the school will always open if we can safely get here. However, this is what to do if there is a substantial amount of snow!
At 6.00 a.m. the Chair of Governors makes the decision with the Head about the quantity of snow and whether it is practical to open. The head informs all radio stations:
Listen to Radio Wiltshire on 103.5, 104.3 or 104.9FM for regular updates on school closures or look on their website www.bbc.co.uk/wiltshire
Listen to GWR or HEART Radio in Wiltshire on 97.2 or 102.2 FM or look on their website www.heart.co.uk/wilthsire
Look on our school website on www.minety.wilts.sch.uk as now that we can update it from anywhere rather than just in school there will be a notice on the first page from 7.00 a.m. onwards as long as the system does not crash with the quantity of messages from U.K. schools.
